title: TSC: a Simple Two-Sided Constraint against Over-Smoothing

problem.claim: Increasing GCN depth can cause over-smoothing, making node representations indistinguishable and submerging initial node features.

gap.claim: Existing solutions mainly address either neighbor-quality effects or neighbor-quantity effects, and seldom address both together.

contributions.claim: Introduces a Two-Sided Constraint for GCNs that combines random masking with a contrastive constraint.
Uses random masking on representation-matrix columns to regulate neighbor information aggregation and a contrastive constraint on rows to enhance node discriminability.
Provides TSC as a plug-in module for GCN and SGC architectures.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on diverse real-world graph datasets reportedly show that TSC reduces convergence of node representations and performance degradation in deeper GCNs.

narrative_sequence.summary: GCNs improve node discriminability by aggregating neighboring information.
Deeper GCNs can use higher-order neighbors but introduce over-smoothing through changing neighbor quality and quantity.
Existing approaches seldom address both identified causes of over-smoothing simultaneously.
TSC combines column-wise random masking and row-wise contrastive constraints as a plug-in module for GCN or SGC.
The authors report improvements on diverse real-world graph datasets, including reduced representation convergence and less degradation in deeper GCNs.

source_observation.claim: The proposed method targets both neighbor-quality and neighbor-quantity mechanisms associated with over-smoothing.

interpretation.claim: Mitigating a failure mode may require constraints that act on distinct mechanisms rather than a single aggregated representation.

application.claim: When designing deep message-passing models, consider separate controls for information aggregation volume and representation discriminability.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported GCN and SGC settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for random masking or the contrastive constraint.
The abstract does not report computational costs, limitations, or sensitivity analyses.
